anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level statements or transaction patterns that force the engine to touch far more data or hold locks longer than business logic requires.
Schema and Index Design Anomaly: Physical table, index, and partition design that fails to support the workload’s access paths, forcing even well-written queries into inefficient scans or lookups.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly: Replication pipeline in which replicas cannot receive or apply log records as quickly as the primary produces them.

When these three root causes coexist, symptoms compound across layers: 1) the primary experiences long-tail query latency, oversized result sets, and extended transaction lifetimes; 2) execution plans show full-table scans, row-by-row lookups, and high index-maintenance overhead; 3) the extra I/O and redo generated by these queries enlarge transaction logs and widen replication lag, with replicas reporting increasing receive, flush, and replay delay; 4) standbys that share the same sub-optimal schema struggle to re-execute the heavy statements, further deepening backlog, while primary log segments cannot be recycled, inflating disk usage and threatening failover freshness.

Causal chain: chatty or bulk-scanning application queries (logic anomaly) encounter missing or non-covering indexes (design anomaly), driving up CPU, I/O, and redo generation on the primary. The larger, longer transactions emitted under this inefficient schema bloat the write-ahead log. Replicas inherit the same schema deficiencies, so their apply threads reproduce the expensive scans and index maintenance, slowing replay throughput below the primary’s production rate (replication anomaly). The resulting lag feeds back to the primary by preventing log truncation and increasing checkpoint and flushing pressure, which in turn amplifies query latency and heightens the probability of further application-level retries—creating a reinforcing loop that degrades both primary performance and replication health.

entry.official_definition: Controls how long STOP REPLICA waits before timing out.
entry.trigger_condition: A STOP REPLICA administrative operation waits longer than rpl_stop_replica_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The administrative replication stop operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when replication endpoints stop exchanging or applying data within the configured timeout window, causing the channel to be considered inactive.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver status, upstream and downstream connectivity, and whether lag or stalled apply is preventing timely progress.
